entities.summary: Henry Mason Mathews was an American military officer, lawyer, and politician in the U.S. State of West Virginia. Mathews served as the seventh attorney general of West Virginia (1873–1877) and the fifth governor of West Virginia (1877–1881), being the first former Confederate elected to the governorship in the state. Born into a Virginia political family, Mathews attended the University of Virginia and afterward practiced law before the outbreak of the American Civil War. When Virginia seceded from the United States, in 1861, he volunteered for the Confederate States Army and served in the western theater as a major of artillery.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the fifth governor of West Virginia and a former Confederate officer, Mathews played a significant role in shaping the state's early history. His tenure as governor from 1877-1881 had lasting regional impact on the development of West Virginia.
